item.title: China Open Source Daily — 2026-11-05
item.description: A Reuters report on 2026-10-20 described openEuler as a distro with a desktop story; four days later the project's kernel repository quietly answered a more interesting question. The canonic home of openEuler's kernel moved from Gitee to AtomGit — the source-forge arm of the same industrial stack — while a mirror named `openeuler-mirror` on GitHub kept publishing, last pushed 2026-11-04, with no issues, no pull requests, 59 stars, and 1,245,880 commits behind it. Reading that mirror's most recent 400 commits against AtomGit's landing page produces two pieces of evidence that point in opposite directions. From GitHub's side (the only side that can be API-queried mechanically) 59 of the last 100 commits are individual, non-CI patches — 45 authored by foreign-mainline maintainers (Google, Meta, NVIDIA, SUSE, AMD, Intel) — and 55 of 100 carry a `From: @...` tag that reveals their real path was an `!NNNNN` merge request on the openEuler forge, reproduced through a bot that signs off as `Tengda Wu <wutengda2@huawei.com>`. From AtomGit's side: 1,849 issues, 1,486 pull requests, 203 members — while GitHub's mirror of the same repository holds exactly zero of each. The 2026-09-30 release, openEuler 26.09, credits 834 contributing developers. The resulting picture is neither fake open source nor an ordinary upstream: a genuinely open downstream that is a locus of decision inside China's procurement market and a mirror everywhere else — and a divergence risk that is visibly small today and structurally large tomorrow.
